title: Angles in Parallel Lines and Polygons
seo_title: Sec 1 Parallel lines and polygons Worksheets: Free Secondary 1 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: angles formed by two parallel lines and a transversal: corresponding angles, alternate angles, interior angles; properties of regular polygons; angle sum of interior and exterior angles of any convex polygon
meta_desc: Free Secondary 1 angles worksheets with diagrams: corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles, interior angle sums, interior and exterior angles of regular polygons and number of sides. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add up to 180°.
key_sub: Interior angle sum = (n − 2) × 180°. Exterior angles add up to 360°.
body_html:
How it works

When a line crosses two parallel lines:

  • Corresponding angles (F shape) are equal.
  • Alternate angles (Z shape) are equal.
  • Co-interior angles (C shape) add up to 180°.

The interior angles of a polygon with n sides add up to (n − 2) × 180°. The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°. For a regular polygon, exterior angle = 360° ÷ n and interior = 180° − exterior.

Example

Find x in the diagram above.

The angles are corresponding (F shape).

Answer: x = 65°

Example

Find the interior angle of a regular pentagon.

Exterior = 360 ÷ 5 = 72°.

Interior = 180 − 72.

Answer: 108°

Common mistakes

  • Thinking co-interior angles are equal. They add up to 180°.
  • Using n × 180° for the angle sum instead of (n − 2) × 180°.
  • Mixing up interior and exterior angles of a regular polygon.
  • Using these rules when the lines are not parallel (look for the arrows).

faq.q: What are corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles?
faq.a: Angles made when a line crosses parallel lines. Corresponding (F) and alternate (Z) angles are equal; co-interior (C) angles add up to 180°.

faq.q: How do I find the sum of the interior angles of a polygon?
faq.a: Use (n − 2) × 180°, where n is the number of sides. A hexagon: 4 × 180° = 720°.

faq.q: How do I find each interior angle of a regular polygon?
faq.a: Find the exterior angle (360° ÷ n) and subtract it from 180°.

faq.q: How do I find the number of sides from an angle?
faq.a: Find the exterior angle and divide 360° by it.

items.q: Why do the interior angles of a pentagon add up to 540°?
c: It can be split into 3 triangles from one vertex
items.e: From one vertex you can draw 2 diagonals, making 3 triangles: 3 × 180° = 540°.

items.q: Can a regular polygon have an exterior angle of 25°?
c: No, because 360 ÷ 25 is not a whole number
items.e: 360 ÷ 25 = 14.4, which is not a whole number of sides. So no.

items.q: An interior angle and its exterior angle add up to…
items.e: They sit on a straight line, so they add up to 180°.

items.q: In a triangle, one exterior angle is 125°. The opposite interior angles are 70° and x. Find x.
items.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: x = 125 − 70 = 55°.
